claimsSupported.claim: The Canal #barra social field included automated away/status messaging that preserved addressability even when a participant was not actively present.
Away scripts could operate as social availability management tools, informing others that messages would be recorded rather than ignored.
Performed presence in IRC should not be reduced to active speech; it may include scripted signals of absence, availability, memory and expected response.

analyticalReading.shortLabel: automated away presence and social availability management
analyticalReading.description: This excerpt shows a scripted away/autoresponder message announcing that the participant is away but that incoming messages will be recorded. The line is valuable because it documents a form of performed presence produced through automation: the participant is not actively speaking, yet the script maintains social addressability, reduces the risk of perceived neglect and signals that interaction can continue asynchronously.
analyticalReading.performedPresenceRelevance: The excerpt supports the concept of performed presence by showing that presence in IRC was not merely online/offline status. It could be communicated by automated messages, away states, scripted replies, message recording and social availability cues.
analyticalReading.socialOrganizationRelevance: The curator notes that -DrNando- was a Canal Barra promoter, associated with VIP lists and social organization. If separately verified, this would strengthen the reading that scripted tools supported practical social coordination, not just technical customization.
analyticalReading.scriptRelevance: The reference to Scøøp Script 2002 indicates use of client-side IRC scripting to manage interaction, attention, response expectations and social continuity.
